questions.stem: Why do phospholipids form a bilayer in water?

options.text: Both heads and tails are attracted to water
The hydrophilic heads face outwards towards water and the hydrophobic tails face inwards away from water
The hydrophobic heads face towards water and the hydrophilic tails face away
Phospholipids are fully soluble in water and stack randomly

questions.explanation: Phospholipids have a hydrophilic (water-loving) phosphate head and hydrophobic (water-hating) fatty acid tails. In water, they arrange into a bilayer with heads facing outward and tails facing inward.
